title: Discovery of antigen and toxin profiles in Clostridioides difficile disease
summary: The aim of this study is to investigate how the C.diff. antigen and toxin can be detected in stool samples in order to reliably distinguish C.diff infected people from healthy or otherwise ill persons . In addition, response or failure to antibiotic therapy should be predicted from changes in antigen/ toxin detection. In addition, DNA and RNA sequencing will be used to create diagnostic profiles of the pathogen spectrum and inflammatory markers within the stool sample in order to determine its microbial diversity. However, sequencing of the human genome is excluded here.

interventions.name: People diagnosed with C.diff; A stool sample is collected on day 0 before administration of the antibiotics and then 24-48 hours later and optionally 10-14 days later.
People suffering from unspecific diaarhea, e.g. after travelling or due to an irritable bowel syndrome as diseased control group. A stool sample is given only at one timepoint
People without diarhea as healthy control group ; A stool sample is given only at one timepoint

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
signed written consent before undertaking any study specific activity 
available for the first two sample time points ( in the C.diff. group); 3rd timepoint is optional
aged between 18-99 years
Exclusion criteria:
unable to provide consent
underlying psychological disease
Hepatitis A diagnosis
